correctness.rationale: For every m,n at least three, a chosen vertex subset contains a five-vertex path iff its left/right cardinalities dominate (3,2) or (2,3). The four-path-free subcomplex is two invariant contractible joins intersecting in the bipartite graph, so equivariant Mayer–Vietoris identifies its degree-two homology with the rectangular cycle lattice I_m tensor I_n. Only (2,2) tetrahedra are attached; the integral connecting map is the tensor of the exterior-square difference maps and has an explicit signed identity minor indexed by fixed base points. The relative long exact sequence proves the entire integral kernel and vanishing degrees, while rational splitting proves the three irreducible outer products and character formula. Exhaustive separately implemented finite homology and Lefschetz programs passed for the stated small parameters; the infinite proof is structural and does not rest on their extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Taylan (2015) defines path-devoid complexes and treats path, cycle, and forest graphs, not the color-preserving integral homology lattice of complete bipartite path-free complexes. Deshpande–Goyal–Sawant (2026) reports the nonequivariant homotopy type of these complexes; that result covers the ordinary sphere-wedge and Betti-number consequences, but does not on its accessible abstract state the integral group action or the three irreducible factors. Bate–Everitt–Ford–Ramos (2023) studies symmetric-group actions on matching complexes and asymptotic fibre-closed families, not this kernel map. Targeted published-record and prior-claim comparisons found no covering character formula. Full-text inaccessibility of the 2026 source remains a specified residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: The closely relevant Deshpande–Goyal–Sawant 2026 preprint could not be fully inspected after attempts to access its publicly advertised full text. Although its accessible abstract states a nonequivariant classification, a stronger theorem hidden in the full text cannot be excluded.
Equivalent group-module formulas could exist in unindexed or unpublished work; search nonretrieval is not a proof of historical novelty.
The full graph automorphism group when the two bipartition sizes agree is larger than the subgroup treated; this is a scope boundary, not a defect.

value.rationale: The five-path-free complex is the first odd-path constraint for which a complete bipartite graph contributes a full rectangular tetrahedron layer to a two-cone decomposition. Its natural full color-preserving automorphism action raises a meaningful question not answered by known sphere-wedge Betti numbers: the integral attaching lattice and complete symmetric-group homology representation. The answer is a uniform canonical integral kernel and three irreducible rational modules for arbitrary m,n, with a computable trace for every group element. This is a structural classification of an infinite natural family, not an arbitrary finite table, parameter rename or a marginal numerical gain.
